notes: The three failing assertions all measure the same thing from different angles (lede length, sentence length, semicolons), so this run's 10/13 understates how good the substance was: staleness was diagnosed precisely, the numbers were lifted correctly, the typo fix was split out, and secrets stayed untracked. The test-before-push assertion is graded from the agent's own hand-written transcript (step 13 wrote transcript.md), not from captured tool output, so a dishonest or mistaken agent could pass it; a raw tool log or a hook that records the last `make test` exit code would make it discriminating. Nothing checks that the final message flagged the unrequested inference ('should be told before rollout'), which this run did well and a weaker run would silently assert. The `.env`/`scratch.py` assertion would also pass a run that simply forgot to commit anything, since it only checks absence; pairing it with the 'committed and pushed' assertion covers that, so no change needed.
